# Feature: Live Browser View

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-069
**Source Plan**: `.spec-lite/plan_ui.md`

While an app-launched run drives a browser, the Mission cockpit shows the **task page** live behind
its glass HUD, so the user can watch what Yantra is doing instead of reading only a timeline. The
view is safe by construction: a screen that might show a secret is never displayed, even when frames
arrive late, when several windows watch at once, or after a reconnect. Frames are never written to
disk and never reach the model, so the live view stays outside the `context.screenshots` grant.
When glass over a moving screencast costs too much, the cockpit switches to Solid on its own. A text
alternative (current host, page title and the RunTimeline) carries the same information for anyone
who cannot or does not want to watch the pixels.

Business value (plan §1, §14): the "glass cockpit over a live browser" is the app's defining
surface; §14 requires "live view ≥ 5 fps within budget, or Solid engages automatically", and §17
resolves critique finding **I8** (screencast safety) through this feature.

**Plan definitions carried verbatim (plan §12 FEAT-069):**

- **Protection** is: the run's `SensitiveScreenLatch` is set (agent secret fills); **or** a
  deterministic secret or masked-value fill is in progress (this feature adds the latch to the
  deterministic fill paths); **or** a FEAT-056 protected control has focus.
- **Frames** carry `{generation, document_epoch, captured_at}`. The worker increments the generation
  on protection set or clear, top-level navigation, target change and stream restart, and drops
  frames from older generations. When protection starts it sends `frames.cleared`; host and app
  discard the displayed image and show "Protected screen — hidden". After protection clears, frames
  resume only from a capture taken after the new generation began.
- **Task page** is the agent controller's active page, following the existing popup policy; a
  switch counts as a target change.
- **Delivery** uses the latest-wins frame queue (§6). Frames are never persisted and never sent to
  the model.

**Interpretations made by this spec (flagged for confirmation, not silent):**

- **"Masked-value fill"** is read structurally as either (a) a fill whose target is a FEAT-056
  protected control (the target descriptor carries `withheld`), or (b) on the agent path, a fill
  whose literal contains a FEAT-FP-008 user-input value (`services.userInput.mask(literal) !==
literal`). A stored-secret fill is the latch's case. A masked-value fill holds protection for the
  fill's duration only, as the plan says ("in progress"); the protected-control focus clause covers
  the time the control keeps focus afterwards.
- **Task page for deterministic runs.** The plan names the agent controller's page. A `run` /
  `resume` workflow drives the executor's single page (`ctx.page`), and §10 requires the
  deterministic secret fill as evidence, so the executor page is the task page for replay runs.
  `ask` / `research` use only FEAT-050 background pool pages, which are **never** screencast
  (ui_brainstorm "task page only"); those runs show the text alternative with a "no live page" state.
- **`frames.state` message.** §6 lists `frames.start/stop`, `frame.ack` and `frames.cleared`. The
  headed, no-page, protected-at-subscribe and unavailable states also need a signal, so this spec
  adds one additive control message, `frames.state`. `frames.cleared` keeps its exact §6 meaning.

## 2. Data Model (Granular)

> `.spec-lite/data_model.md` does not exist. This feature has **no persisted entities**: frames,
> generations and protection state are in-memory and live only on the wire. The entities below are
> protocol schemas (Zod, `@yantra/protocol`) and run-local runtime state.

### Entities & Attributes

- **ScreencastFrameMeta** (protocol; the `meta JSON` part of a type-`0x02` frame payload, §6)
  - `generation` (int ≥ 0) — the worker's frame generation at capture. NOT NULL
  - `frame_seq` (int ≥ 0) — monotonic per run stream, used for acks. NOT NULL
  - `document_epoch` (int ≥ 0 | null) — the task page's top-level committed-document epoch at
    capture; null only when unreadable
  - `captured_at` (string, ISO-8601 UTC) — capture instant from CDP `metadata.timestamp`. NOT NULL
  - `width`, `height` (int > 0) — decoded JPEG dimensions (device-independent px)
  - `.strict()`; encoded meta is at most 1 KiB
- **FramePayload** (protocol codec, not a schema): `[meta_len: u16 BE][meta JSON (UTF-8)][JPEG
bytes]`, total at most 4 MiB (§6); the JPEG part must start with the SOI marker `\xFF\xD8`.
- **FramesStart** `frames.start` (client → worker / app → host)
  - `max_width` (int 320–1920, default 1280), `max_height` (int 240–1200, default 800)
- **FramesStop** `frames.stop` — no fields
- **FrameAck** `frame.ack`
  - `generation` (int), `frame_seq` (int)
- **FramesCleared** `frames.cleared` (worker → host → app)
  - `generation` (int) — the generation that began with protection; every frame below it is void
  - `reason` (enum `protection`) — closed; extended only by a protocol change
- **FramesState** `frames.state` (worker → host → app; additive, see §1)
  - `generation` (int)
  - `state` (enum `live | protected | headed | no_page | unavailable`)
  - `reason` (enum `capture_failed | incompatible_worker | protection_unverifiable | none`)
  - `page` (`{host: string ≤ 253, title: string ≤ 200}` | null) — sanitized, for the text
    alternative; null while `protected` and when no page exists
- **FramesSubscribe / FramesUnsubscribe** (app → host JSON-RPC, §6 `frames.subscribe {run_id}`)
  - `run_id` (string, run-id grammar)
- **Capability** string `frames/1`, advertised in the D17 `hello {capabilities}` handshake by
  workers that can serve frames.
- **ScreenProtection** (core, run-local, in memory, never persisted, never model-visible)
  - `latch` (`SensitiveScreenLatch`) — the existing run latch, now observable
  - `holds` (count of open fill holds, each with `reason: 'masked_fill' | 'secret_fill'`)
  - `focus` (`'clear' | 'protected' | 'unknown'`) — from the focus guard; `unknown` counts as
    protected (fail closed)
- **FrameGate** (core, per run stream, in memory)
  - `generation` (int), `generationStartedAt` (ms, injected clock), `protected` (bool),
    `lastEpoch` (int | null), `nextFrameSeq` (int)
- **LiveViewState** (app store, per window per run, in memory)
  - `state` (`connecting | live | protected | headed | no_page | unavailable | reconnecting`)
  - `generationFloor` (int) — highest generation from `frames.cleared` / `frames.state`
  - `page` (`{host, title}` | null), `lastDrawn` (`{generation, frame_seq}` | null)

### Relationships

- Run 1:1 ScreenProtection (owned by the agent controller, or by the replay `ExecutionContext`)
- Run 1:0..1 active screencast stream (exists only while ≥ 1 client sent `frames.start`)
- Stream 1:1 FrameGate; Stream 1:N per-client one-slot frame queues (worker side)
- Host run attachment 1:N subscribed windows, each with its own one-slot queue and generation floor

### Indexes & Constraints

- **Generation is monotonic** per run stream and never resets while the worker lives; a restart of
  the stream is itself a generation increment.
- **Generation floor rule** (every hop: worker, host, app): drop any frame whose `generation` is
  below the highest generation announced by `frames.cleared` or `frames.state`.
- **Fresh-capture rule:** a frame is admitted to generation G only if `captured_at` ≥ the instant G
  began; a frame without a readable timestamp is dropped.
- **Persistence constraint:** no frame byte is written to any file (run directory, `host.log`,
  `runtime.jsonl`, provider session, temp files). Enforced by the TASK-012 byte scan.

### TASK-003: Screen protection — observable latch, fill holds, and the deterministic fill paths

- [ ] **Implementation**: (1) Add `subscribe(listener: (latched: boolean) => void): () => void` to
      `SensitiveScreenLatch`: notify `true` synchronously inside `latch()`, `false` when
      `isLatched()` clears on an epoch change and in `clearOnTeardown()`. Existing semantics
      (fail-closed on unreadable epoch, clear only by epoch change or teardown) stay byte-for-byte.
      (2) Add `packages/core/src/browser/screen-protection.ts`: `ScreenProtection` composes the
      latch, a hold counter (`hold(reason): Release`, release idempotent) and the focus state
      (`setFocus('clear' | 'protected' | 'unknown')`); `isProtected(currentEpoch)` is true when the
      latch is latched **or** holds > 0 **or** focus is not `clear`; `subscribe(listener)` fires
      synchronously on every transition of the combined value. (3) `AgentBrowserController` owns
      `public readonly screenProtection = new ScreenProtection(this.sensitiveScreenLatch)`.
      (4) `createExecutionContext` creates a run-local `SensitiveScreenLatch` and
      `ScreenProtection` on the replay context. (5) Deterministic fill paths: in
      `step-handlers/fill.ts` and `fill-element.ts` (`driveFillElement`), call
      `ctx.sensitiveScreenLatch.latch(ctx.settler?.epoch ?? null)` **after** the secret resolves
      and **before** any character is dispatched; a thrown fill leaves the latch set (same rule as
      the agent path). For a masked-value fill (target descriptor carries `withheld`, see §1),
      wrap the fill in `const release = ctx.screenProtection.hold('masked_fill')` released in
      `finally`. (6) Agent path: in `applyBrowserFill`, hold `masked_fill` for the literal path when
      the target carries `withheld` or `services.userInput?.mask(literal) !== literal`; the secret

### TASK-005: Frame gate — generations, fresh-capture admission and clear signals

- [ ] **Implementation**: Add `packages/core/src/live-view/frame-gate.ts`, a pure state machine
      with an injected clock: `FrameGate` with `generation`, `onProtectionChanged(protected)`,
      `onNavigationCommitted(epoch)`, `onTargetChanged()`, `onStreamRestarted()` and
      `admit({capturedAtMs, documentEpoch}) → {kind: 'forward', meta} | {kind: 'drop', reason}`.
      Rules: every one of the four events increments `generation` and stamps
      `generationStartedAt = clock()`; while protected, every frame is dropped
      (`reason: 'protected'`); otherwise a frame is admitted only if `capturedAtMs ≥
generationStartedAt` (`'stale_capture'`) and its timestamp is present (`'no_timestamp'`).
      Protection start returns a `cleared` signal carrying the new generation; protection clear
      and the other events return a `state` signal. The gate assigns `frame_seq`. It holds no

### TASK-007: Live-view hub — per-client latest-wins delivery, states, and orchestrator wiring

- [ ] **Implementation**: Add `packages/core/src/live-view/live-view-hub.ts`. One `LiveViewHub` per
      run, created by whoever runs the handler and passed down as an optional dependency
      (`liveView?: LiveViewHub`) to the agent orchestrator and `RunOrchestrator`, which call
      `hub.attach(taskPageSource)` once the source exists. Clients (`hub.addClient(sink)`) call
      `start({max_width, max_height})`, `stop()` and `ack({generation, frame_seq})`. The hub starts
      the `ScreencastSource` and the focus guard only while ≥ 1 client is started (zero cost
      otherwise), stops both when the last client stops, and treats every restart as
      `onStreamRestarted()`. It subscribes to `ScreenProtection`: on protection start it **first**
      empties every client's frame slot and calls `sink.control(frames.cleared)`, then stops the
      screencast (pixels stop at the source, not only at the gate); on clear it restarts the
      screencast under the new generation. Each client has one frame slot (latest wins) and an
      in-flight flag; a frame is offered to the sink only after that client acked its previous
      frame. `frames.state` is sent on start and on every state change: `live`, `protected`,
      `headed` (the source page is headed; no screencast), `no_page` (no task page yet or
      background-only run), `unavailable` (`capture_failed` or `protection_unverifiable`). `page`
      is `{host, title}` read on navigation commit, title truncated to 200 characters and passed
      through the run's sanitizer (`public` profile) when present; `null` while protected. Hub
      failures are caught, logged once at `warn` with the reason code, and turn into
      `frames.state unavailable`; the run continues unaffected. Logging records lifecycle and
      counts only, never frame bytes or titles.

### TASK-009: Host relay — `frames.subscribe`, per-window slots and the binary WebSocket lane

- [ ] **Implementation**: In the FEAT-065 host add `live-view-relay.ts`. RPC `frames.subscribe
{run_id}` (authenticated window capability required, run must be attached) registers the window
      and returns the current `frames.state`; `frames.unsubscribe` and window close unregister.
      The host sends `frames.start` to the worker when the first window subscribes to that run and
      `frames.stop` when the last leaves. Worker frames are acked to the worker **on receipt** and
      placed in each subscribed window's one-slot queue (latest wins), so one slow window cannot
      throttle another. The host keeps a per-window **generation floor**: on `frames.cleared` it
      purges every window slot below the new generation and forwards the message on the JSON-RPC
      text lane immediately; frames below the floor are dropped. Frames go to a window as **binary
      WebSocket messages** (the TASK-002 payload) only when that window acked its previous frame and
      `ws.bufferedAmount` is under a small threshold (64 KiB), so JSON-RPC responses and events
      never wait behind a frame. A worker without `frames/1` (D17) yields
      `frames.state unavailable/incompatible_worker`. Frames are never written to `host.log`;
      the log records subscribe/unsubscribe and counts only.
- [ ] **Unit Tests**: with a fake worker channel and fake WebSockets: a delayed frame of an older
      generation arriving after `frames.cleared` is dropped for every window; multiple windows
      each receive `frames.cleared`; a stalled window keeps receiving JSON-RPC responses promptly
      and does not slow a second window; a window without a valid capability cannot subscribe;
      first subscriber starts, last unsubscribe stops; a host log after a session contains no JPEG
      SOI bytes and no page titles; an incompatible worker fixture yields `unavailable`.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: Invoke **Document** update mode for the architecture document (host
      relay and backpressure).
- **Verify**: the FEAT-065 host suite plus the relay suite pass; the FEAT-065 security suite still
  passes with the new RPC methods.
- **Depends on**: TASK-008, FEAT-065

## 6. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth**: Frames reach the app only over an authenticated window session (FEAT-065 per-window
  capability on the JSON-RPC WebSocket) and an authenticated run socket (FEAT-064 token in the
  first message). `frames.subscribe` without a valid capability is rejected; an unauthenticated run
  socket client receives nothing. No new endpoint, cookie or URL is introduced; frames never use
  signed artifact URLs.
- **Privacy and model boundary**: Frames are never persisted (TASK-012 byte scan) and never sent to
  the model (no tool or prompt path imports `live-view`; TASK-012 boundary test), so the
  `context.screenshots` grant and Vision Assist rules do not apply (plan §7). Only the task page is
  captured, never FEAT-050 pool pages. Protection is fail-closed at three hops (worker gate and
  source stop, host floor, app floor at draw time); `unknown` focus and an uninstallable guard are
  treated as protected. Page titles are sanitized and rendered as text only (plan §7, untrusted
  page-derived text).
- **Error Handling**: The live view is best-effort and isolated from the run: every live-view
  failure becomes a `LiveViewError` with a closed code (`CAPTURE_FAILED`,
  `FOCUS_GUARD_UNAVAILABLE`, `PAYLOAD_INVALID`) mapped to `frames.state unavailable` with a reason,
  and never changes a run's outcome, exit code or artifacts (TASK-007 characterization). Malformed
  frame payloads are dropped and counted; a malformed outer frame closes the connection (FEAT-064
  rule). No error is swallowed silently: each is logged once per stream.
- **Logging**: Worker: Pino `debug` for stream start/stop and generation bumps (counts and reason
  codes only), `warn` once per failure code. Host (`host.log`): frame subscription start/stop per
  run with window counts. Never logged anywhere: frame bytes, page titles, captured URLs beyond the
  host already in run events, launch codes or capabilities. No new `runtime.jsonl` event kinds
  (plan §11 lists none for the screencast).
- **Performance**: Zero capture cost when no client is started; Chrome-side ack pacing caps capture
  at the target fps; latest-wins slots and generation floors bound memory to one frame per client
  per hop; frames never delay control traffic (TASK-008, TASK-009). Targets: ≥ 5 fps, app main
  thread < 15 % of one core, or automatic Solid (TASK-011).
- **Accessibility**: Text alternative always available; canvas has an accessible name; state
  changes announced politely once; no focus movement on live updates (plan §9); `axe-core` on every
  state (I9 evidence).
- **Cross-platform**: Run sockets (named pipes on Windows, Unix sockets elsewhere) and real-Chrome
  cases run on Windows, macOS and Linux CI.
